findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the fallback-URL config source: state whether it is built from `vars.GERRIT_SERVER`/`inputs.GERRIT_PROJECT` or from the action's `gerrit-url`/`gerrit-project` inputs, and confirm the resulting URL equals `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/rebar`.
evidence: Prose: 'the fallback URL form is https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/rebar'
Step 2: 'fetch the same refspec from https://${{ vars.GERRIT_SERVER }}/${{ inputs.GERRIT_PROJECT }}'
The two references name different config keys (gerrit-url/gerrit-project inputs vs vars.GERRIT_SERVER/inputs.GERRIT_PROJECT) for the same value
findings.finding: The fallback Gerrit fetch URL is described two different ways: the 'Fix plan' prose derives it from action inputs `gerrit-url: https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com` plus `gerrit-project: rebar` (yielding `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/rebar`), but implementation step 2 constructs it from `https://${{ vars.GERRIT_SERVER }}/${{ inputs.GERRIT_PROJECT }}`. It is unstated whether `vars.GERRIT_SERVER` equals `rebar.solutions.navateam.com` and whether `inputs.GERRIT_PROJECT` equals `rebar`, so the executor cannot be sure which config source produces the correct fallback URL.
scenarios: Executor writes the workflow using vars.GERRIT_SERVER but the actual value differs from the gerrit-url the action consumed, producing a fallback URL that never resolves the refspec
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one authoritative source and use it consistently in both the prose and step 2; e.g. define the fallback URL as `https://${{ vars.GERRIT_SERVER }}/${{ inputs.GERRIT_PROJECT }}` and add a note asserting these evaluate to `rebar.solutions.navateam.com` and `rebar` respectively.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm (against the pinned action source / Gerrit HTTP config) that the Gerrit-direct fallback fetch to https://GERRIT_SERVER/GERRIT_PROJECT is anonymously fetchable, or specify the credential the reimplemented fallback must pass.
evidence: Plan: 'the fallback URL form is https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/rebar' with no credential/auth clause
ADR-0021 §3 confirms the fallback exists ('falls back to fetching directly from the Gerrit server') but does not state the fetch is anonymous
T3 checklist item (c): 'Auth/HTTPS preconditions stated' — the plan states HTTPS but not the auth posture of the Gerrit HTTP endpoint
findings.finding: The plan asserts the Gerrit-direct fallback fetch URL is `https://${{ vars.GERRIT_SERVER }}/${{ inputs.GERRIT_PROJECT }}` (an anonymous HTTPS git fetch) but does not state the auth/HTTPS precondition — whether Gerrit's HTTP git endpoint permits an anonymous fetch of `refs/changes/*`. Gerrit's smart-HTTP git access is frequently authenticated; if so, the plan's plain `git fetch <https-url> <refspec>` fallback would fail while the pinned action may supply credentials the reimplementation omits.
findings.location: Fix plan, implementation step 2 ('fetch the same refspec from https://${{ vars.GERRIT_SERVER }}/${{ inputs.GERRIT_PROJECT }}')
scenarios: On replication lag the mirror fetch misses and the fallback runs against an auth-gated Gerrit HTTP endpoint, failing where the pinned action would have authenticated

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State (and verify against the pinned action source / repo visibility) whether the reimplemented GitHub-mirror fetch needs the GITHUB_TOKEN extraheader that actions/checkout normally sets on `origin`, or that navapbc/rebar's `refs/changes/*` mirror is anonymously fetchable over HTTPS.
evidence: Plan: 'the workflow will recreate that source explicitly as https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}.git in the initialized workspace'
.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:549 references 'an `origin` remote being configured by the checkout action', implying the action manages origin/credentials the plan reimplements
ADR-0021 Consequences call the change refs 'visible on the public GitHub mirror' (suggesting public) but the plan states no anonymous-fetch precondition
findings.finding: The plan's step-1/step-2 GitHub-mirror fetch — a fresh `git init` plus `git remote add origin https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}.git` — does not state whether an anonymous HTTPS fetch of the change refspec succeeds, i.e. whether it carries the auth the pinned action's `origin` normally has. Under actions/checkout the `origin` remote is configured with a GITHUB_TOKEN extraheader; a bare re-created origin drops that credential. If navapbc/rebar's mirror fetch is token-gated, the reimplemented step-2 mirror fetch fails auth and falls straight through to the Gerrit fallback (or fails outright), diverging from the action being replaced.
findings.location: Fix plan, implementation steps 1-2 ('add origin=https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}.git', 'Fetch GERRIT_REFSPEC into FETCH_HEAD from origin')
scenarios: The rebar GitHub mirror requires a token for git fetch; the hand-rolled origin fetch 401s and the lane silently degrades to the Gerrit fallback or aborts

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Weigh (and justify against) the narrower alternative of keeping the SHA-pinned checkout-gerrit-change-action and inserting a pre-checkout FETCH_HEAD/input-pair assertion, versus hand-rolling this lane's own fetch+fallback plumbing.
evidence: Plan: 'Replace only this workflow's first checkout step with explicit shell plumbing equivalent to the pinned action's fetch protocol' — reconstructs behavior rather than reusing it

checkout-gerrit-change-action is SHA-pinned and reused across gerrit-verify.yaml, _build-and-test.yml, _optionality.yml, _mutation.yml, _eval-discipline.yml, _artifact-probe.yml, jira-dc-capability-map.yml
ADR-0021: the action's mirror-first-then-Gerrit-fallback is an intentional, alarmed contract; hand-rolling risks drifting from it
findings.finding: A structurally-simpler, lower-blast-radius alternative is not weighed: KEEP the pinned checkout-gerrit-change-action and add a pre-checkout consistency check (validate the GERRIT_REFSPEC↔GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION input pair, or assert FETCH_HEAD == GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION) instead of hand-rolling this lane's own fetch/fallback protocol from inferred action source. The chosen approach diverges this one lane from ~9 other uses of the SHA-pinned action and re-implements a fetch protocol the plan admits it is only reconstructing from the action's source.
findings.location: Fix plan (steps 1-5) / 'Replace only this workflow's first checkout step'
scenarios: The third-party action's fetch protocol changes at a future pin bump; the hand-rolled copy in this lane silently drifts

findings.suggested_fix: Keep the pinned action, and add a guard step that fetches GERRIT_REFSPEC (mirror-first, Gerrit fallback per ADR-0021) and fails if git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD^{commit} != GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION before the action-driven checkout, preserving the shared protocol.
